description: The model's active articles become ONE listing with variations on one Amazon store — Amazon's "variation family"; call it a model with variations when talking to the user: a parent whose SKU is the model's code (no price, no quantity) and a child listing per article, varying by colour and/or size — the theme is chosen from what the Amazon product type declares. An article not yet on the store becomes a new child (action create); an article already sold there as a listing of its own — a model put on a store article by article, or copied from another store without its parent — is JOINED to the parent (action attach): only parentage_level, child_parent_sku_relationship and variation_theme are sent to it, by PATCH under the SKU Amazon knows it by (amazonSku when that differs), and its offer, photos and texts stay as they are. A listing Amazon already shows under this parent counts as in the family (skipped, listed). Every listing is first validated by Amazon (VALIDATION_PREVIEW); this tool only checks and creates nothing. Start from gaps: one entry per kind of problem with every SKU it concerns, found before Amazon is asked — size or color (set with update_product), price (none in the run's currency, the marketplace's: upsert_product_prices, set_product_channel_price or apply_bulk_price_change), productType (update_category), brand, images, condition, title; quantity with blocking=false: the article does not track stock, so the listing goes up without one (update_product with trackInventory, then adjust_stock); and barcodeLength with blocking=false: the article's barcode has another number of digits than the rest of the model, so a digit may be lost — confirm it from the label before publishing (update_product with ean). Amazon is asked only when no gap blocks. A listing that cannot be joined gets status excluded and holds nobody up — the rest of the model goes ahead, it stays a listing of its own, and every later run tries it again; the gap cannotAttach (blocking=false) lists them. Its reason is attachProblem — otherParent (on this store it is already a variation of another parent: never moved, settle it in Seller Central), productType (Amazon lists it under another specific product type than the family's category: fix the category's Amazon product type with update_category, or the listing in Seller Central) or notOnStore (the CRM records it on this store but Amazon has nothing under its SKU: refresh with inspect_amazon_listings refresh=true and check again — it then becomes a new child) — or, with no attachProblem, issues: Amazon's own dry run refused the join (a listing Amazon holds under its generic type PRODUCT is asked under the family's type and Amazon answers here). If Amazon refuses a join for a missing colour or size, fill them with update_amazon_listing_content parts ["attributes"]. Status blocked always comes with this article's own missing or issues; waiting means the article has nothing wrong and the run stopped on another article's gap or the model's blocker. Also returns parentSku, theme, currency, blocker (tooFewArticles, noAxis, missingAxisValue, duplicateCombination, themeUnsupported, parentSkuTaken, parentTitleTooLong, tooManyArticles — the last is this CRM's limit for one run, not Amazon's: never suggest splitting the model), fieldProblems (what the product type still needs per Amazon's schema, once per field: attribute key, title in the marketplace's language, kind missing or invalid, allowed values with labels, units, the SKUs concerned, and for an attribute made of several values its parts: each part's key attribute.part, title, required, allowed values and unresolved — true when neither a person nor the CRM has an answer for it), parentIssues, children per article (missing, quantity, barcode, Amazon's sentences, status; notChecked = Amazon did not get to it, call again — what passed is kept for an hour while the article's data stays the same, so each call only checks the rest) and skipped articles (already on Amazon, taken off the channel). The CRM fills model_name, list_price, the dimensions and a size attribute (from each article's own size, with its system and class) itself; set any other field, or a part reported as unresolved, with set_amazon_field_values on the model (every article inherits it) — keys and values from get_amazon_fields. Then create it with publish_amazon_variation_family.

marketplaceId.description: One Amazon store by its id. Omit for the main store; for a write with several stores open it is required. Each store holds its own family, in its own language.

modelId.description: A product model id (the model a product's modelId points at; get_product shows it).

name: check_amazon_variation_family
title: Check a model with variations for Amazon
